summary.value: The Bergische Kräher is an old German chicken from the Bergisches Land, a hilly region east of Düsseldorf and Cologne. Its name means Bergish crower, and it belongs to the long crowing group of breeds: a cock's crow can last up to five times longer than an ordinary rooster's. Local clubs have held crowing contests for centuries, judging each crow for length and beauty, and a breed society has existed since 1884. The accepted color is gold laced black, with slate blue legs, a single comb and white earlobes. Cocks weigh roughly 6.5 to 7.5 pounds and hens 4.5 to 5.5 pounds. It is a dual purpose bird with good meat, and hens lay about 130 medium white eggs a year and seldom go broody. Only a few hundred birds remain, so it suits conservation minded keepers who do not mind a loud rooster.
